title: How a “Duck Hunt” Led to the Federal Reserve
body_text: In November 1910, six powerful men made their way to Jekyll Island, off the coast of Georgia, for a duck hunt. Jekyll Island was known for its abundant wildlife and structures made from tabby, a coastal cement mixture of lime, water, sand, ash, and broken oyster shells. The guest list included Nelson Aldrich, a powerful Senator from Rhode Island and Chairman of the U.S. Senate Finance Committee; A. Piatt Andrew, Assistant Secretary of the Treasury Department; Henry Davison, Partner at J.P. Morgan and an advisor to the National Monetary Commission; Arthur Shelton, Secretary of the National Monetary Commission; Frank Vanderlip, President of National City Bank (today's Citi Bank); and Paul Warburg, Director of Wells Fargo & Company. The duck hunt turned out to be a ruse. Instead, these titans of the business and political worlds had come together to carve out a plan to reform the young nation's banking system. The U.S. economy had been continuously disrupted by a series of banking crises and reoccurring nationwide panics. Ultimately, the plans these men set out for a central banking body at this secret gathering on this secluded island became the Federal Reserve. The significance of the Jekyll Island meeting wasn't revealed until years after the Federal Reserve Act was passed in December 1913. The Federal Reserve System, or Fed, is the central bank of the U.S., and its purpose is to promote the effective operation of our economy. It's made up of 12 regional banks and a Board of Governors consisting of seven people. The Board of Governors oversees 12 Reserve Banks and is directly accountable to Congress. Appointed by the President, the Fed Chair is the designated head of the Board of Governors. The 12 Reserve Banks are spread across the country, and Missouri is the only state with two official banks, one in St. Louis and the other in Kansas City. Since its inception in 1913, the Fed has only had 16 different leaders with many Fed chairs having presided over multiple administrations. Janet Yellen became the first woman to hold the position on February 3, 2014, and Jerome Powell is the current Chair having been appointed on February 5, 2018. The Fed's top concern is the effective operation of the U.S. economy. It promotes financial system stability, supervises and regulates financial institutions and activities, works to promote a safe and efficient system for U.S. dollar transactions, and promotes consumer protection and community development. However, it's best known for conducting the nation's monetary policy. Conducting Monetary Policy Monetary policy is the management of the nation's money supply and credit to promote maximum employment and stable prices for goods and services. The Fed controls the supply of money mainly by raising or lowering the federal funds rate. Lowering the rate boosts other asset prices if the economy is sluggish or inflation is too low. Raising the rate may be necessary if the economy is overheating or inflation is too high. These changes will then affect the spending decisions of households and businesses. Promoting Financial System Stability To keep the financial system stable, the Fed monitors the relationships between investors, savers, borrowers, and businesses – both in the U.S. and outside the country. Their goal is to make financial institutions and markets more resilient, so they can bend without breaking during times of distress. For example, during WWII the Treasury and the Federal Reserve worked together to help finance the war. It was necessary for the military to purchase ships, airplanes, vehicles, guns, and ammunition, in addition to recruiting, training, and deploying millions of soldiers across six continents. The 12 Federal Reserve Banks organized Victory Fund committees to market war bonds to direct the savings of American citizens into the war effort. The majority of the bonds issued were in small denominations, $25 or less. The Treasury also asked the Federal Reserve to hold interest rates at low levels to keep the costs of the war down. When the terrorist attacks occurred on September 11, 2001, the Fed found the planning and training they had previously developed to deal with the Y2K bug invaluable. They quickly moved to assure bankers and investors that they would continue to provide lending to keep the economy going. In the days that followed, the Fed lowered interest rates and loaned more than $45 billion to financial institutions in order to provide stability to the U.S. economy. During the Great Recession from December 2007 to June 2009, the Fed took some nontraditional approaches. It kept the federal funds rate at an exceptionally low level for an extended period of time with the intention of providing monetary stimulus. It also implemented credit-easing programs to keep credit flowing and reduce its cost. Finally, the Fed took the unusual step of purchasing mortgage-backed securities (MBS) and the debt of housing related U.S. government agencies to provide support for the housing market, which was at the center of the crisis and recession. Supervising and Regulating Financial Institutions The Fed regulates and supervises a broad range of financial entities, including bank holding companies, state member banks, savings and loan holding companies, foreign banks operating in the U.S., and others. It issues specific regulations and guidelines governing the formation, operations, activities, and acquisitions of these financial entities. It also is involved in monitoring and examining these entities to make sure they operate in a safe and sound manner. The Fed will take formal action against any institution that violates the rules, including cease and desist orders and civil money penalties. Fostering Payment and Settlement System Safety and Efficiency The Fed provides services to the federal government and depository institutions and is the banker for the U.S. Treasury. The Reserve Banks provide the U.S. Treasury with a checking account, and the Fed processes payments and deductions from the Treasury's account. Much of this is done electronically through the Treasury Direct system. While the Treasury produces U.S. paper money and coin, it's the Fed's job to put newly produced money into circulation. It's also their responsibility to destroy money that is no longer fit for circulation. When money makes its way into a Federal Reserve Bank, the Fed assesses the quality of the currency and orders its destruction if it's not up to standard. The average $1 bill remains in circulation for nearly 6 years, the average $10 bill lasts for only 4.5 years, and the life expectancy of a $100 bill is around 15 years. Promoting Consumer Protection and Community Development The Fed also keeps a watchful eye on financial institutions to make sure they follow the laws that protect consumers. These consumer credit laws help ensure that financial institutions are acting in the public's best interest. The Truth in Lending Act, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act, and the Truth in Savings Act are all examples of consumer credit laws. In addition, the Fed conducts extensive research, analysis, and data collection to identify emerging consumer financial issues and their implications. While there are 12 Federal Reserve Banks, the New York Federal Reserve Bank has the highest status. The New York Fed is the largest in terms of assets and volume of activity and has several unique responsibilities. For one, it is responsible for conducting open market operations, which is the buying and selling of outstanding U.S. Treasury securities. To carry out exchange rate policy, it buys and sells dollars as directed by the U.S. Treasury. One of its most noted responsibilities is the storage of gold for the U.S. government, foreign governments, other central banks, and official international organizations. The New York Fed Bank building is located in the Financial District of Manhattan, New York City on 33 Liberty Street. It was constructed between 1919 and 1924 and occupies the full block. Its vault rests on bedrock, 80 feet below street level, and contains the world's largest depository of gold, estimated to be 508,000 gold bars weighing approximately 6,350 tons in 2015 . The Fed has kept the federal funds rate relatively low for an extended period of time. When the Fed decides to push up rates, consumers looking to purchase a home or who have adjustable-rate mortgages could pay more on their loans. Although a Fed rate increase doesn't directly affect mortgage rates, it does impact the 10-year Treasury bond, which is tied to mortgage rates. Consumers looking to purchase a home should consider doing it sooner rather than later, and homeowners with adjustable-rate mortgages may want to consider refinancing to a fixed-rate loan. When the Fed raises its rate, banks quickly follow by increasing their prime rate. Since most credit cards come with variable rates tied to the prime rate, consumers may want to pay down their credit card debt to avoid paying higher rates. An increase in Fed rates also means increased interest rates for student loans and auto loans. As with mortgage loans, the sooner a consumer can lock in a rate, the better. Few people would have expected that a secret meeting on an isolated Georgia island would lead to the birth of a U.S. institution that is the most powerful single actor in the nation's economy. Yet, for over 100 years, the Fed has played a crucial role in American life, from influencing interest rates, to monitoring the economy for signs of trouble, to fining companies that aren't following the rules, to promoting community development. title: DRDGOLD converts favourable gold price into cash generation and long-term reinvestment
body_text: Media releases DRDGOLD converts favourable gold price into cash generation and long-term reinvestment Details Published: Wednesday, 18 February 2026 07:44 Key features Operating profit increased by 72% for the period to R2 712.8 million Headline earnings increased by 99% for the period to R1 932.4 million Interim cash dividend of 50 SA cps (H1 FY2025: 30cps) R1 651.3 million of capital expenditure funded from operating cash flows 67 million tonne Kloof #2 mine dump added to FWGR resources Gold production decreased by 9% to 2 337 kilograms Johannesburg, South Africa. 18 February 2026. DRDGOLD Limited (JSE: DRD, A2X: DRD, NYSE: DRD) reported interim results for the six months ended 31 December 2025 (comparative period: 6 months ended 31 December 2024) marked by materially higher cash generation, disciplined reinvestment and continued progress on projects designed to extend the life of its operations. Revenue increased by 33% for the period to R5 053.2 million from the sale of 2 388kg of gold (H1 FY2025: 2 567kg) as the average gold price received rose 43% to R2 114 227/kg. As an unhedged producer, DRDGOLD captured the full benefit of the higher gold price, resulting in headline earnings of R1 932.4 million, up 99%, and operating profit of R2 712.8 million, an increase of 72%. Throughput tonnages decreased by 4% to 12.5Mt (H1 FY2025: 12.9Mt) due mainly to rain and weatherrelated interruptions in November and December 2025. Despite lower production, free cash inflow increased to R793.1 million (H1 FY2025: R319.0 million), enabling the Group to fund capital reinvestment of R1 651.3 million entirely from operating cash flows. Cash and cash equivalents increased to R1 734.4 million (H1 FY2025: R661.2 million), while an interim cash dividend of 50 cents per share was declared (H1 FY2025: 30 cents per share). “Favourable gold prices have allowed us to reinvest meaningfully in extending the life of our operations, to maintain a strong financial position and to continue to create value in a way that remains sustainable for our business and our stakeholders,” said CEO, Niël Pretorius. Operational performance Group gold production declined by 9% to 2 337kg (H1 FY2025: 2 564kg), primarily due to a decrease in the yield to 0.188g/t (H1 FY2025: 0.199g/t) and rain and weather-related interruptions in November and December 2025. Cash operating costs increased to R980 042/kg (H1 FY2025: R866 221/kg), while all-in sustaining costs rose to R1 094 188/kg (H1 FY2025: R963 316/kg), reflecting lower gold production and higher input costs. The operating margin expanded to 53.7% (H1 FY2025: 41.5%), supported by higher gold price realisation. Advancing Vision 2028 DRDGOLD continued to progress the projects underpinning Vision 2028, aimed at unlocking its extensive tailings resource base, increasing production and extending operating life well beyond 2040. At Ergo, construction of infrastructure linking the Ergo plant to the Daggafontein tailings storage facility (TSF) is nearing completion, with first deposition anticipated in the first quarter of FY2027. Regulatory and engineering work required to restart deposition at the Withok TSF also progressed during the period. At Far West Gold Recoveries (FWGR), growth capital expenditure of R1 290.0 million supported continued progress on the DP2 plant expansion, the regional tailings storage facility (RTSF) and associated pipeline infrastructure. Commissioning of the expanded DP2 plant remains on target for the first quarter of FY2027. The Group’s resource base increased following the transfer of approximately 67 million tonnes of goldbearing tailings from Sibanye-Stillwater to FWGR at the Kloof 2 dump. Managing complexity, risk and operational resilience Operational resilience improved during the period. Electricity costs at Ergo declined by 23% despite Eskom tariff increases, reflecting the contribution of the Ergo solar plant and battery energy storage system (BESS). Production was not disrupted by an industry-wide sodium cyanide shortage due to proactive risk identification and mitigation. The Group has also concluded a five-year wage agreement at its Ergo operations, bringing certainty for employees and operational stability through guaranteed annual wage increases, performance-linked incentives and enhanced employee support measures. “Our business must have the flexibility to survive the lean times, and to take full advantage of the good times,” Pretorius said. “That means reinvesting in our assets, managing costs and risk, strengthening energy security, maintaining stable labour partnerships and making decisions that keep the business resilient and competitive over the long term.” Looking forward DRDGOLD continues to prioritise the execution of Vision 2028, using current market conditions to secure the long-term sustainability of its operations while planning for the inevitable cyclicality of gold markets. title: U.S. Tax Treaties: A Guide to Preventing Double Taxation
summary: U.S. tax treaties reduce double taxation and clarify taxing rights on cross-border income. Learn PE rules, residency tie-breakers, withholding rates, MAP, and LOB tests.
body_text: Cross-border income is more common than ever in 2026. Remote workers, foreign investors, multinational royalties, and globally mobile founders all run into the same question: which country gets to tax this, and how much? Left unanswered, the same dollar can be taxed in two places at once. That's the problem U.S. tax treaties exist to solve. A U.S. tax treaty is a bilateral agreement between the United States and a foreign country designed to minimize double taxation and prevent fiscal evasion. In practice, treaties assign taxing rights between the two countries, reduce or eliminate withholding on cross-border payments like dividends, interest, and royalties, and give taxpayers a clear framework for claiming relief. At their core, treaties overlay certain domestic tax rules with a shared set of rules that both countries agree to honor, so a taxpayer can determine the correct treatment of a given stream of income with confidence. Most U.S. treaties are modeled on the U.S. Model Income Tax Convention (the most recent U.S. Model was released in 2016) or the OECD Model Tax Convention, which is why they share a familiar article-by-article structure. This guide walks through how treaties work, why they matter for tax professionals and their clients, the most recent developments to watch heading into 2026, and how to pin down the exact withholding rate for a cross-border payment in seconds using TaxGPT's AI tax research . Why Tax Treaties Matter Tax treaties are a critical component of international tax research and often interact with the principles of federal tax research . Without tax treaties, cross-border taxpayers face: Full taxation by both countries on the same income stream Uncertainty about which country has primary taxing rights Higher withholding taxes on dividends, interest, and royalties Risk of disputes without a clear resolution mechanism While our Ultimate Guide to Tax Research introduces the concept, this guide provides a deeper analysis of how to locate and apply specific treaty provisions in practice. What Are the Key Articles in a U.S. Tax Treaty? Although each U.S. tax treaty reflects the specifics of its bilateral relationship, most U.S. treaties follow a consistent structure inspired by the U.S. Model Income Tax Convention (the “U.S. Model”). The most recent U.S. Model was released in 2016. Within that structure are several foundational articles that serve as the backbone for resolving cross-border tax questions. These provisions define who is taxed, where they’re taxed, and to what extent they’re taxed, making them essential for treaty-based planning and compliance. Below is an overview of the most relied-upon treaty concepts and how they are applied in practice. Residency and Tie-Breaker Rules (Article 4 of the U.S. Model) Article 4 sets the criteria for determining whether an individual or entity qualifies as a resident of a treaty country, a prerequisite for claiming most treaty benefits. However, dual residency is not uncommon. A person may meet domestic residency tests in both countries due to physical presence, citizenship, domicile, or other ties. To resolve this, tax treaties apply a sequence of tie-breaker rules, which assign residency to a single jurisdiction by evaluating: Where the person has a permanent home The location of their center of vital interests Their habitual abode Nationality And if necessary, a competent authority agreement Establishing treaty residency is often document-driven. Taxpayers typically need to submit a tax residency certificate and possibly other disclosures to benefit from reduced withholding rates or to avoid double taxation. Permanent Establishment (PE) (Article 5 of the U.S. Model) The concept of a Permanent Establishment (PE), defined in Article 5, is one of the most consequential in treaty interpretation, especially for multinational enterprises. A PE generally refers to a fixed place of business through which the operations of a foreign enterprise are conducted in the treaty partner country. Its existence determines whether the country in which the income is generated has the right to tax the foreign company’s business profits. Common examples of a PE include: A branch or office A place of management A factory or workshop A construction site that exceeds the time threshold specified in the treaty Importantly, treaties often carve out exceptions for activities that are preparatory or auxiliary in nature, such as warehousing, order processing, or display facilities, which do not constitute a PE. This distinction is critical in managing international tax exposure. Without a PE, a foreign business is typically shielded from tax on its business profits in the other jurisdiction. Withholding Tax Reductions (Articles 10, 11, 12 of the U.S. Model) One of the most practical benefits of tax treaties is the ability to reduce or eliminate withholding taxes on passive income streams. Articles 10, 11, and 12 specifically address: Dividends Interest Royalties These articles may override the standard 30% withholding rate imposed by U.S. domestic law, often reducing it to a lower rate, depending on the specific relationship between the payer and recipient and the provisions of the applicable treaty. For example, under Article X of the Canada–U.S. tax treaty, a U.S. subsidiary paying dividends to a Canadian parent corporation (owning at least 10% of voting stock) may qualify for a 5% withholding rate instead of the default 30%. To claim these benefits, the recipient must meet relevant Limitation on Benefits (LOB) provisions and provide accurate documentation, typically Form W-8BEN-E, accompanied by a tax residency certificate. Getting the rate right also reduces the risk of downstream issues like refund delays, penalty exposure, and treaty-based return disputes. Mutual Agreement Procedure (MAP) (Article 25 of the U.S. Model) When countries disagree on how to apply treaty provisions, or when a taxpayer is subject to double taxation despite treaty protections, Article 25 provides a formal path to resolution known as the Mutual Agreement Procedure (MAP). This article allows a taxpayer to request intervention from either country’s competent authority if they believe the treaty is not being applied correctly. MAP is commonly invoked when: Both countries assert taxing rights over the same income Residency status is unclear or disputed PE determinations lead to unexpected taxation A reduced withholding rate is denied Key elements of the MAP process: Under the U.S. Model, there is no specific timeframe in which to file a MAP request. However, in some treaties, the taxpayer must generally file within three years of first being notified of the contested action Competent authorities from both countries attempt to reach an agreement outside of judicial proceedings In transfer pricing matters, MAP often overlaps with Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) MAP reinforces the treaty's role as a living dispute-resolution mechanism, not just a set of static rules. While these core articles form the foundation of most treaties, the U.S. model includes several unique provisions that practitioners must understand to apply them correctly. What Are the Most Important U.S.-Specific Treaty Clauses? While most tax treaties share a common model, U.S. tax treaties introduce distinctive provisions that reflect national policy objectives. These uniquely American clauses require close attention, as they often override or limit the availability of treaty benefits. The Saving Clause The Saving Clause, present in nearly all U.S. treaties, preserves the right of the United States to tax its own citizens and residents as if the treaty didn't exist. - Purpose: Ensures U.S. persons cannot avoid taxation by moving abroad - Applies to: U.S. citizens, green card holders, and some long-term residents - Exceptions: treaty-specific This clause makes the U.S. an outlier globally, as most countries relinquish taxing rights under treaty-based residency assignments. It is also why U.S. citizens generally must keep filing US taxes as an expat even after establishing residency elsewhere. The Limitation on Benefits (LOB) Article The LOB article is a comprehensive anti-abuse rule designed to prevent treaty shopping. It ensures only legitimate residents of a treaty country can claim treaty benefits. Key Tests: Publicly-Traded Test Active Trade or Business Test Ownership and Base Erosion Test Derivative Benefits Test Failure to meet these tests can result in denial of treaty benefits, even when a payment would otherwise qualify under treaty provisions. Proper documentation and LOB classification on Form W-8BEN-E are critical when making a treaty-based return position. What Are the Latest Developments in U.S. Tax Treaties? The global tax landscape is evolving faster than ever. As countries renegotiate treaty terms to reflect digital economies, minimum tax standards, and geopolitical shifts, staying informed about U.S. tax treaty developments has become essential for proactive international tax planning. Here are the most significant updates and ongoing changes affecting U.S. tax treaties in 2025 and 2026. New & Pending Treaties In recent years, the U.S. Senate has shown renewed interest in treaty approvals after a prolonged pause. One major milestone: The U.S.–Chile Tax Treaty Ratified in 2023 and entered into force in 2024 This treaty is especially relevant for energy, mining, and tech sectors, which have heavy cross-border investment between the two nations Introduces standard provisions, including reduced withholding tax rates and Permanent Establishment thresholds Contains a Limitation on Benefits (LOB) article to prevent treaty abuse Its implementation marks the first new U.S. tax treaty to be ratified in over a decade Other Developments The U.S.–Hungary Treaty ceased to have effect for payments made or taxable periods beginning on or after January 1, 2024. Bilateral discussions continue on provisions involving digital services, investment income, and base erosion safeguards Some treaties may undergo revisions to align with Pillar Two norms, though progress varies by country Pillar Two & the Multilateral Instrument (MLI) The OECD's Pillar Two framework, which imposes a 15% global minimum tax on large multinational groups, has had ripple effects on tax treaty interpretation, especially for provisions affecting tax credits, PE thresholds, and MAP access. The U.S. has not signed the OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI), a tool many countries use to quickly update their treaties to align with BEPS (Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) principles. However, many U.S. treaty partners have adopted the MLI, leading to treaty mismatches. For example, the Canada–U.S. tax treaty remains untouched by the MLI, but Canada has modified other treaties via MLI clauses, creating inconsistencies that practitioners must reconcile. Practical Implications: Review each treaty to see how it interacts with Pillar Two. Expect possible FTC limits in the U.S. , especially for top-up taxes in Pillar II countries. Update structures to avoid friction between legacy treaty rules and the new minimum-tax regime. Having instant access to specific treaty articles, withholding tax rates, and compliance triggers transforms international tax from a reactive burden to a proactive strategy. To see how this capability can be applied across your entire client base, keep reading.

title: Key Takeaways from the Zoox Case Study
summary: Exploring the benefits of consolidating contract workers under a single employer of record
body_text: Exploring the benefits of consolidating contract workers under a single employer of record ‍ HireArt recently published a case study describing a major workforce consolidation from several different agencies and employers serving California-based autonomous vehicle company Zoox. The project consolidated siloed groups of contract workers supporting Zoox into a single platform for employment–namely, HireArt. This case study examines challenges in maintaining a positive employment experience amidst growing program complexity, important factors in simplifying contract workforce programs, and what can ultimately result from improving worker happiness. The following are three key takeaways from the case study. ‍ Program Complexity Affects Worker Happiness ‍ It’s not uncommon for a contract workforce program to be supported by multiple different staffing agencies and employers of record. As programs grow and mature, so too does the level of complexity in managing it. Multiple vendors means multiple points of contact, multiple systems with which to interface, and multiple schedules to consider for the approval and submission of timecards. This has an impact on the workers themselves, who are counting on a smooth onboarding process, timely communication response, and consistent pay, and it is reflected in industry-typical worker net promoter scores (NPS), which hovered at around +28 in 2023. ‍ Workforce Consolidation Is Beneficial, But Challenging ‍ Handling employment through a single agency as opposed to multiple agencies seems like a simple solution to address growing program complexity, but there are a lot of important considerations to make when migrating workers to one platform. Accruals - Workers have saved up PTO and sick days that must be migrated to the incoming EOR. Regulatory Compliance - Zoox has operations across the United States that are each subject to regulatory requirements from the local and state levels, which would need to be supported. VMS Integration - Zoox uses a vendor management system (VMS) provided by VNDLY, which means any incoming EOR would need to integrate with that system. ‍ Worker Happiness Creates Measurable Outcomes ‍ Happy workers feel inspired to do their best work each day, but does that translate into positive outcomes that can be measured? The answer is yes. Among the group of 88 workers that transitioned to the HireArt platform, there was a 90% retention rate. Additionally, Zoox’s contract workforce program through HireArt continued to grow 270% by the end of 2023. One vehicle operator from that group had this to say: “We feel taken care of and like the good communication. Definitely would recommend this agency.” Consolidation of contract workers under HireArt resulted in an efficient, compliant, and worker-friendly contract workforce program, contributing to Zoox’s operational growth and high worker satisfaction. ‍ Click here to read the full case study. ‍

title: Comscore en bref : la finance en ligne en Europe
summary: Dans l’édition de cette semaine de Comscore en bref, nous analysons la consommation liée aux services financiers en Europe. Notre analyse inclut des statistiques sur la France, l’Allemagne, l’Italie, l’Espagne et le Royaume-Uni.
body_text: Dans l’édition de cette semaine de Comscore en bref, nous analysons la consommation liée aux services financiers en Europe. Notre analyse inclut des statistiques sur la France, l’Allemagne, l’Italie, l’Espagne et le Royaume-Uni. Périmètre : Nous incluons des sites web et des applications mobiles qui fournissent des services financiers tels que le paiement en ligne, opérations bancaires, bourse, assurance, finance personnelle et investissements. Par exemple, PayPal et BNP Paribas. Faits saillants : Tableau 1 : En Italie, Espagne et le Royaume-Uni, plus de 80% de la population digital a accédé à un site web ou application liée à la finance en août 2020. Néanmoins, dans la plupart des marchés, l’incertitude économique liée à la COVID-19 semble impacter d’une manière négative le nombre de visites sur les sites financiers par rapport à l’année dernière. L’Italie a résisté à cette tendance avec 6.6% de personnes en plus utilisant ces services par rapport à l’usage de l’année dernière. Tableau 2 : Le marché de la finance en ligne est très concurrentiel : des banques traditionnelles (telles que BNP Paribas en France ou Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe en Allemagne, etc.) et des jeunes startups (telles que Klarna, Monzo ou Revolut) rivalisent pour une part de marché. Ainsi, de nombreuses entreprises ont atteint 1% ou plus de l’audience. Quelques-unes d’entre elles – mais représentant toujours une part significative – ont atteint plus de 5% de l’audience, soit un internaute sur vingt. Il n’est pas clair si le marché européen peut soutenir un si grand nombre d’acteurs de la finance en ligne. L’incertitude économique due à la pandémie devrait conduire à une certaine consolidation de ces acteurs dans les années à venir. Tableau 2 : Comparé à la région Asie-Pacifique, en Europe, les banques et les entités financières physiques dominent le paysage des services financiers et bancaires. Parmi les pure players numériques, Paypal est sans doute celui qui a le plus réussi. Tableau 1 . title: IDEX Health & Science Champions Giving Back to Local Communities
summary: In 2021, our Life Science Optics team supported local food banks, holiday toy drives, rebuilding of shelters for those who are homeless, and more
body_text: Rochester, New York, March 11, 2022 – IDEX Health & Science’s Life Science Optics Team—comprised of units in Rochester, NY Lima, NY and Carlsbad, CA—donated $104,998 in 2021 to local organizations (surpassing their initial goal of $100k). Working in conjunction with the IDEX Foundation, a charitable organization made up of customers, employees, and shareholders, participants consistently strive to create value and improve the communities where their teams live and operate. IDEX Health & Science aims to “see a need and fill it,” like with the dual monetary donation and goods donation drive for the Willow Domestic Violence Center. “[IDEX’s] generous donation supports Willow’s life-changing, and life-saving, programs and services,” wrote Meaghan de Chateauvieux, President & CEO of Willow Domestic Violence Center. “It is donors, like you, who ensure that Willow can support survivors of domestic violence when they need us the most.” In 2021 alone, the Life Science Optics (LSO) Team was able to support food banks, holiday toy drives, rebuilding of shelters for those who are homeless, and the backpack donation drives for local students (to name a few). Notably the LSO Team, partnered with the IDEX Foundation, donated almost $29.9K to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Rochester to support educational programs with new equipment, software, supplies, additional staff, field trips, and the opportunity for a weekly STEM class with an engineer from their Rochester facility. After receiving just under 500 backpacks filled with supplies, Assistant Principal Tiffany Lee said: “On behalf of Roberto Clemente School #8, thank you for the generous donation of book bags and supplies. title: CFL athletes receive integrity training as part of industry-wide effort to safeguard Canadian sport
body_text: A new integrity training programme has been delivered to Canadian Football League (CFL) teams, bringing together the sport, betting operators, data and integrity specialists in a coordinated effort to better protect CFL athletes and staff from match manipulation and fraud. The programme, led by the CFL’s official data partner, Genius Sports, and the International Betting Integrity Association (IBIA), the leading betting integrity monitor in Canada, included face-to-face trainings, allowing for direct engagement with players and more open discussion about the pressures and risks they may encounter. Athletes across all nine CFL teams have taken part in the training sessions, including those in Edmonton and Calgary, both based in Alberta, which is due to launch its new licensing model for sports betting and gaming on 13 July. The sessions also included teams Toronto and Hamilton, based in Ontario, which was the first Canadian province to open its market to private operators in 2022. IBIA has been approved as an integrity monitor in both provinces, working together with the gambling regulators in those jurisdictions. The in-person trainings were delivered by IBIA’s Education Ambassador, Jean-François Reymond, former NFL, CFL and EFL player Anthony Mahoungou, Genius Sports’ Head of Integrity Operations, Stephen Emberson and Special Counsel for Sports Integrity, Natalie St Cyr Clarke. The sessions included the IBIA’s 3Rs approach: Rules, Responsibility, Report. Jean-François, as a former professional athlete, brought direct insight into the realities players face, the situations where integrity can be tested and the best approach to engaging with athletes. “In-person training reflects a simple reality: integrity measures don’t work on paper alone, they work when athletes understand them, trust them, and use them,” he stated. The training focus on practical scenarios, helping athletes to identify, resist and report approaches linked to match-fixing, the misuse of inside information and other forms of betting-related corruption. By prioritising prevention through education, the programme aims to address risks before they escalate. Khalid Ali, CEO of IBIA , said: “Sport’s integrity is only as strong as the investment and cooperation behind it. When leagues, athletes, operators and integrity bodies work together, and education truly connects, it moves from theory into action, creating a powerful tool to help athletes to recognise and respond to risks in real situations.” Stephen Emberson said “In the fight against betting-related corruption, education is an essential pillar to safeguarding both the participants and the competitions themselves. These workshops provided an invaluable platform to speak directly with the CFL players, demonstrating how individuals may seek to manipulate markets and the exact measures they should take to report anything suspicious. Having the opportunity to deliver education in person, on topics such as social media risks, and gambling related harm, gave Genius Sports and the IBIA the opportunity to full engage with the participants and giving them the tools to protect themselves and the league.” “The integrity of our game is paramount,” said the CFL’s Associate Vice President, Health & Safety and Football Operations. “Working with our partners and industry leaders, while delivering in person training, reflects the commitment of the league, betting operators and integrity specialists to educate players and staff on match manipulation, its impacts and how to respond if confronted with it. There is no place for it in our game, and we will continue to take every step necessary to protect the CFL.” The initiative reflects a broader approach across sport and betting towards prevention as the most effective way to protect integrity. By addressing risks early, through education, awareness and direct engagement with athletes, stakeholders aim to reduce opportunities for misconduct before they arise. The impact extends beyond the dressing room, helping to safeguard competitions and regulated betting markets while protecting the credibility of sport as a whole. IBIA’s involvement in this initiative is part of a CAD $300,000 investment committed by IBIA and its members FanDuel, bet365 and Betway to support integrity education and prevention measures in Canadian sport. That will include a third consecutive year of player education, conducted alongside PFA Canada, for Canadian Premier League (CPL) players and staff later this year.

title: Rainmaker and Atmo Announce Strategic Alliance to Transform Weather Modification With AI-Powered Precision Cloud Seeding
summary: Partnership Combines Radar-Driven Robotic Cloud Seeding with Ultra-Precise AI Meteorology to Fight Water Shortages Worldwide
body_text: Rainmaker and Atmo Announce Strategic Alliance to Transform Weather Modification With AI-Powered Precision Cloud Seeding ‍ Partnership Combines Radar-Driven Robotic Cloud Seeding with Ultra-Precise AI Meteorology to Fight Water Shortages Worldwide ‍ EL SEGUNDO, CA and SAN FRANCISCO, CA – July 14, 2025 – Rainmaker Technology Corporation, the pioneering cloud seeding company, and Atmo, Inc., the leader in AI-based ultra-precise meteorology, today announced a strategic alliance to restore water supplies worldwide. The alliance creates the world's most advanced weather modification platform by uniting two of the most innovative companies in atmospheric science. By combining Rainmaker's radar-validated cloud seeding platform with Atmo's ultra-fast, highly-accurate AI weather simulations, the partnership will deliver measurable precipitation enhancement with unprecedented precision and cost-effectiveness. ‍ "This alliance represents the future of weather technology," said Alexander Levy, CEO of Atmo. "Atmo's AI will identify optimal conditions for cloud seeding with unprecedented precision, while Rainmaker's drones can act on those insights immediately. Together, we'll ensure no opportunity is missed to restore water supplies worldwide." ‍ "We're deploying an end-to-end solution from forecast to rainfall," said Augustus Doricko, CEO of Rainmaker. "For the first time, we can combine AI meteorology with radar-validated cloud seeding operations to deliver measurable precipitation enhancement with extreme accuracy and cost-effectiveness. ‍ From Forecast to Rainfall: How the Integrated System Operates Under the strategic alliance, Rainmaker will integrate Atmo's AI weather forecasting and simulation capabilities into its operations, enabling: Radically Improved Targeting: Atmo's ensemble deep learning models, which predict weather up to 40,000 times faster and up to 100x more precisely than conventional weather models, will enable Rainmaker to identify optimal seeding conditions with unprecedented accuracy Multi-Simulation Optimization: Advanced scenario modeling will optimize precipitation outcomes by simulating thousands of potential seeding strategies in real-time Real-Time Effect Measurement: Atmo's continuous weather monitoring combined with Rainmaker's proprietary radar validation system will provide real-time measurement of seeding effectiveness Customer Weather Intervention Options: Atmo will offer its customers a comprehensive menu of weather modification interventions, provided and conducted by Rainmaker, to mitigate drought and severe weather impacts ‍ Breakthrough Technologies Driving the Alliance ‍ Rainmaker's Innovation: The company has developed the only sub-55-pound drone capable of flying in severe icing conditions, enabling effective seeding in supercooled liquid conditions at orders of magnitude lower cost than traditional aircraft operations. Rainmaker's internally designed and manufactured radar system provides unprecedented measurement and attribution of precipitation from cloud seeding operations, enabling real-time physical measurement of seeding effects with exceptional precision. ‍ Atmo's AI Advantage: Named one of TIME's Best Inventions, Atmo's AI meteorology system learns from over 60 years of climate data and is continuously updated with data from numerous satellites, ground stations, and radars. The AI models are up to 100 times more detailed and 40,000 times faster than traditional supercomputer-based forecasting, enabling precision weather simulation at unprecedented resolution and speed. Atmo AI meteorology systems are already used daily by governments, militaries, and enterprises worldwide. ‍ Immediate Benefits at Scale for Governments & Enterprises Worldwide ‍ Both Atmo and Rainmaker specialize in delivering transformative results at regional and national levels, and the alliance will deliver enhanced capabilities to both companies' extensive customer bases. The teams have identified significant synergies in their customer bases, with opportunities to cross-sell combined capabilities to governments and institutions worldwide. When Atmo identifies a client needing precipitation enhancement, Rainmaker can deliver. When Rainmaker encounters a customer requiring advanced weather simulation and forecasting, Atmo provides the solution. "We realized that solving weather challenges requires partnering at scale, " noted Levy. "By combining Atmo and Rainmaker's networks and expertise, we can now offer governments a complete weather prediction and modification system that no one else can match. ""We're both trailblazers in atmospheric science," added Doricko. "This partnership allows us to share opportunities globally and ensure that no institution has to choose between knowing what weather is coming and being able to influence it. They can have both." ‍ Rainmaker's current customers include the Utah Department of Natural Resources, Colorado Department of Natural Resources, Oregon Department of Agriculture, and cities throughout Texas and California. Atmo's current customers include the Republic of the Philippines, Tuvalu, the United Nations, US Air Force, and US Navy. ‍ Addressing the Critical Global Challenge of Water ‍ The partnership addresses urgent global needs as extreme weather events and drought conditions intensify worldwide. Drought has been the most expensive cause of loss nationally at $56.6 billion, making up 35 percent of all crop insurance payouts in recent years. Insurance payments to farmers due to drought rose more than 400% between 1995 and 2020 to $1.65 billion annually, while in 2022, the program's most expensive year on record, crop insurance subsidized 62% of policyholder premiums at a cost of $12 billion. Africa alone has experienced $70 billion in drought-related economic losses in the past 50 years. The Rainmaker-Atmo alliance delivers advanced weather intervention capabilities to address these mounting costs through: Enhancing water security through measurable precipitation increases Mitigating drought impacts on agriculture and water supplies Reducing severe weather risks to critical infrastructure Providing cost-effective weather modification at scale ‍ Market Impact and Future Expansion ‍ The alliance positions both companies at the forefront of the emerging weather modification market. Rainmaker's recent $25M funding round and cost-effective operations (approximately $50 per flight hour including materials) combined with Atmo's global track record operating AI meteorology systems and recognition as a TIME Best Invention create a powerful platform for rapid market expansion. ‍ The partnership will initially focus on North American and Pacific operations, with plans to expand globally as regulatory frameworks develop for precision weather modification services. ‍ ‍

title: Carbon Offsets 101
summary: Overwhelmed by the concept of carbon offsets? Here's where to start.
body_text: A carbon offset is an effort to counterbalance some amount of carbon emissions. Someone pursues a project that either removes carbon dioxide that's already in the atmosphere or to prevents future carbon emissions from ever reaching the atmosphere. Offset projects exchange money for "carbon credits"—a relationship that demands due diligence. Typically, whoever manages the project receives funding from someone else—someone who wants to "offset" some carbon emissions. The core idea here is that, since global warming is a global problem, it doesn't matter where reductions happen. In exchange for their payment, the funders receive a "carbon credit." To become " carbon neutral ," a company needs to hold enough credits to match their total carbon emissions. This indicates that they have helped fund sufficient carbon avoidance and removal to neutralize their climate impacts. The "offset" is a project that removes or avoids carbon emissions. The "credit" is tradable paperwork that certifies an offset has happened. The offset concept was first introduced in the 1990s, and since then has exploded in popularity. According to the classification system used by the United Nations, there are more than 200 kinds of offset projects—thousands of different efforts across the globe. The wide world of offsets As noted above, these projects can be divided into two big categories. Some projects actively remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. The most inexpensive way to do this is to plant trees, which soak up CO2 to fuel their own growth. It's also possible to remove atmospheric carbon using technology that directly pulls molecules from the air. Offset projects fall into two categories: some remove carbon from the atmosphere, others avoid future carbon emissions. The second category of offset projects avoids emissions. One common example is the destruction of industrial gases. Certain gases (like refrigerants) have a potent greenhouse effect; unused gases sometimes just sit in tanks that are slowly leaking into the atmosphere. Some companies search for such tanks and incinerate their contents. You can find a deeper dive into the various categories of offsets in this post . Gas tanks slowly release their contents, many of which have a greenhouse effect. Photo by Carl Nenzen Loven on Unsplash. A question of trust You may have heard stories about problematic offset projects. For example, there are decades-old forest reserves that are now registered as offset projects—which means the owners are getting paid to "keep" trees that they never intended to cut down. Various organizations are attempting to weed out problematic offset projects—with varying degrees of success. Such projects are not "additional"—that is, they would have existed even if the carbon offset money did not arrive. That means whoever gets a credit for the project has not actually offset their emissions. There other ways other ways that projects can go wrong, too. This post explores some of the key traits that distinguish truly effective offsets from the rest. Hawk Mountain Sanctuary in Pennsylvania has been registered as a carbon offset project—even though the forest has already been protected for decades. Photo credit: Zeete , licensed under Creative Commons. To help address these issues, it's important to have someone vet and verify projects. The Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) was launched by the UN in the 1990s as a part of the first major carbon offset market. The point of the market was to allow countries more flexibility as they pursued the emissions-reduction requirements mandated by the Kyoto Protocol, the world's first binding climate-change treaty. The CDM has been criticized, though, for being far too lax. Subsequently, many other crediting organizations have appeared, often targeting corporations that are voluntarily pursuing offset projects. For a fuller account of these organizations and their history, see this post . Read this next: The many types of pollution October 5, 2020 · Climate knowledge

title: Can we replace our data warehouse with Claude connectors?
summary: I built our full marketing funnel report with AI connectors. No warehouse, no analyst. It works and it's efficient. It just doesn't scale past me.
body_text: Last week I built our entire top-of-funnel report by myself. No data team, no ticket in a queue, no month-long project. Two days, and well... it works. I connected Claude to HubSpot, PostHog, and Common Room, asked questions in plain English, defined what each metric actually means, and ended up with a dashboard the whole team now uses. No warehouse and no pipeline. As someone who lives and breathes the world of pipelines, semantic layers and data quality, all of this felt like a crime. So before I called the warehouse dead, I sat with it and worked out what actually makes sense here and what doesn't. So you really didn't centralize anything? No. And that's the part that actually changed. The old rule was simple: centralize everything into a warehouse, model it, then ask your question. Connectors flip the order. Through MCP the model reaches into each source where the data already lives and answers across all of them, so there's nothing to centralize first. That's a new starting point for analytics, and it's the one real shift here. But didn't the AI do the hard part? Less than you'd think. Once the connectors are wired up, the querying takes care of itself. The part I had to own and manage was what every number actually meant. Almost every raw count in our CRM is wrong. Not broken, just misleading. A metric I figured would be trivial turned out to be full of existing-customer activity and duplicate logs, and meant nothing until I pinned it to one source. A field that looks like it tells you where a lead came from actually hides it. Count naively and you sweep in test addresses and bots that auto-add themselves to calls. None of that is carelessness I cleaned up after. Raw data just looks like this until someone decides what to count. Fine, but it's reproducible, right? For me, yes. I turned the definitions into reusable skills, so next month I run the same report and get the same numbers. But repeatable and reliable aren't the same thing. A skill is a copy of a definition, not the definition. It reproduces my report when I ask my question, my way. It does nothing for the question I didn't think to anticipate. So just share the skill with everyone? That makes it worse, not better. Copy a skill to ten people and you have ten definitions. Someone edits theirs, someone's a version behind, someone writes a new one for a question mine never covered. There's no canonical number anymore, just the most recent one in the room. And a skill can't tell you when it's wrong. The day HubSpot renames a field or a dbt model changes grain, it keeps running the old logic and hands back a confident, wrong number. Nobody gets alerted. You find out when someone notices the funnel looks off, if they notice. A shared copy is still a copy. Hand it around and the drift spreads with it. Then commit it to a repo and share it that way? That solves distribution, not drift. Version control stops everyone keeping their own divergent copy, which is real. But the skill reaches straight into the raw systems, and it carries all the cleaning I did by hand: which rows to drop, which source to trust, what to exclude. Pinning that logic to sources that keep changing, and keeping it correct for every question the org throws at it, is the hard part. A repo hands everyone the same file. It doesn't keep the logic true as the data underneath moves. That's the work modeling and a semantic layer do. So can you replace the warehouse with connectors, or not? For my own questions, honestly, yes. It was fast, it was efficient, and I'd do it again tomorrow. For the company's reporting, no. It worked because I knew the data cold, and it stays reliable only as long as I'm the one asking. The moment the answer has to serve someone who doesn't know the sources, the whole thing has to stand on more than a skill on my laptop. Two things a skill can't replace. The first is the data foundation. Something still has to move the data, clean it, and land it somewhere built for querying, not your production database. I got away without a warehouse because I shaped how every source is modeled in the first place. At org scale you don't get that for free, and democratizing analytics doesn't retire data ownership, it leans on it harder. There's also the bill. For my handful of questions, reaching into the raw sources each time costs almost nothing. For a whole org asking all day, and agents asking on everyone's behalf, paying to pull and re-interpret raw data on every query adds up fast. Model the data once and query that, and it's cheaper, not just cleaner. The second is shared meaning. What counts as a lead, what to exclude, which source is the truth. Those definitions have to come out of my skills and into one place the whole org, and every agent, reads from. One person's shortcut isn't a shared answer until it lives in a semantic layer and a governance layer. That's the design principle behind Elementary, and an agent needs two things before it answers. Whether the data is trustworthy: is the table fresh, did its dbt models pass their tests, are there nulls where there shouldn't be. And what the data means: which source is the truth, what counts as a lead, what to leave out, the business context that turns a raw column into the right number. Elementary's context engine is the single place both of those live, for every person and every agent, so the answer doesn't depend on who's asking. Miss either half and you still get a confident wrong number, just faster. So when would you actually use this? Both, for different jobs. For the questions that carry weight, the ones a decision or a board number rests on, route them through the modeled, governed stack where the answer is owned and checked. For fast, low-stakes exploration, connectors are perfect: when you want to see whether a trend is even real before you invest in standardizing and cleaning the data behind it, a marginal mistake costs almost nothing, and you get the answer in minutes instead of a sprint. Used this way, connectors are how you decide what's worth putting in the warehouse in the first place. You can ask your data anything now. The real question is whether everyone else, and every agent, gets the same answer you did.

title: OCR de Estados Financieros: de PDF a datos estructurados
summary: En el acelerado mundo empresarial actual, la capacidad de analizar estados financieros de manera rápida y precisa es esencial para mantener una ventaja competitiva. La tecnología de Reconocimiento Óptico de Caracteres (OCR) ha evolucionado significativamente, pasando de la simple conversión de texto a la extracción de información estructurada, independientemente del formato del documento. Este avance permite a las empresas obtener métricas financieras clave como la razón corriente, margen neto, margen de EBITDA y el debt to asset ratio, esenciales para evaluar la salud financiera de una organización. En este artículo, exploraremos cómo el OCR de Trébol está transformando el análisis financiero, la importancia de prevalidar los documentos y cómo la integración con motores de decisión potencia la toma de decisiones estratégicas.
body_text: OCR de Estados Financieros: de PDF a datos estructurados ‍ En el mundo financiero actual, la capacidad de analizar estados financieros de manera rápida y precisa es esencial para mantener una ventaja competitiva, especialmente para las empresas de servicios financieros. La tecnología de Reconocimiento Óptico de Caracteres (OCR) ha evolucionado significativamente, pasando de la simple conversión de texto a la extracción de información estructurada, independientemente del formato del documento. Este avance permite a las empresas obtener métricas financieras clave como la razón corriente, margen neto, margen de EBITDA y el debt to asset ratio, esenciales para evaluar la salud financiera de una empresa. En este artículo, exploraremos cómo la inteligencia artificial de Trébol permite realizar análisis financieros de manera más rápida y sencilla, la importancia de prevalidar los documentos, cómo realizar una conversión sencilla de PDF a Excel, los desafíos al analizar múltiples estados financieros, la variedad de formatos de estados financieros, la precisión de la extracción y la capacidad de integración mediante APIs para potenciar la toma de decisiones estratégicas. ‍ OCR Tradicional vs. OCR de Estados Financieros de Trébol ‍ Limitaciones del OCR Tradicional ‍ El OCR tradicional se enfoca en convertir imágenes de texto en texto digital, pero presenta limitaciones significativas al aplicarse a estados financieros: Dependencia del Formato : Cualquier variación en el diseño o estructura del documento puede resultar en errores de extracción. Datos No Estructurados : No distingue entre diferentes tipos de información, dificultando su uso directo en análisis financieros. Procesamiento Superficial : Incapaz de interpretar contextos financieros o identificar métricas clave. ‍ Ventajas del OCR de Estados Financieros de Trébol ‍ El OCR de Estados Financieros de Trébol supera estas limitaciones al: Extraer Información Estructurada : Independientemente del formato, identifica y extrae datos financieros específicos. Adaptabilidad al Formato : Reconoce patrones y elementos clave sin importar las variaciones en el diseño de los estados financieros. Integración con Análisis Financiero : Proporciona directamente las métricas financieras esenciales para el análisis y la toma de decisiones. Alta Precisión de Extracción : Utiliza algoritmos sofisticados que mejoran la exactitud de los datos extraídos, reduciendo errores y aumentando la confiabilidad de la información. Conexión mediante APIs : Permite la integración fluida con otros sistemas y plataformas, facilitando la automatización y escalabilidad del proceso. ‍ Conversión de PDF a Excel, caso sencillo ‍ Una de las funcionalidades básicas pero cruciales del OCR de Estados Financieros de Trébol es la capacidad de convertir documentos PDF a Excel de manera sencilla. Este proceso facilita la manipulación y análisis de datos financieros al estructurarlos en hojas de cálculo editables. La conversión se realiza automáticamente, permitiendo a los usuarios obtener tablas y gráficos precisos sin necesidad de intervención manual, lo que ahorra tiempo y minimiza errores. ‍ Conoce más del OCR de Estados Financieros en Video ‍ Retos al Analizar Múltiples Estados Financieros ‍ Sin embargo, cuando se trata de analizar grandes volúmenes de estados financieros, el proceso se vuelve más complejo. La diversidad en los formatos, estructuras y terminologías utilizadas en diferentes documentos puede dificultar la estandarización y el análisis coherente de los datos. Aquí es donde el OCR de Estados Financieros de Trébol demuestra su verdadero potencial al manejar estas variaciones de manera eficiente, permitiendo un análisis masivo sin comprometer la precisión. ‍ Diversidad de Formatos de Estados Financieros ‍ Los estados financieros pueden presentarse en una variedad de formatos y estilos, dependiendo de la industria, la región y las normas contables aplicadas (como NIIF, GAAP, entre otras). Esta diversidad representa un desafío significativo para la extracción de datos. El OCR de Estados Financieros de Trébol está diseñado para reconocer y adaptarse a estos diferentes formatos, asegurando que la información relevante sea extraída correctamente sin importar las variaciones en el diseño o la estructura del documento. ‍ Precisión de la Extracción ‍ La precisión en la extracción de datos es fundamental para cualquier análisis financiero. Los errores en la interpretación de cifras o en la identificación de métricas clave pueden llevar a conclusiones erróneas y decisiones empresariales equivocadas. El OCR de Estados Financieros de Trébol utiliza técnicas de aprendizaje automático y procesamiento de lenguaje natural para mejorar continuamente la precisión de la extracción, minimizando los errores y asegurando que los datos extraídos sean fiables y exactos. ‍ Extracción de Métricas Financieras Clave ‍ El OCR de Estados Financieros de Trébol permite la extracción automática de métricas críticas que son fundamentales para evaluar la salud financiera de una empresa: Razón Corriente Definición : Mide la capacidad de la empresa para pagar sus obligaciones a corto plazo con sus activos corrientes. Importancia : Una razón corriente mayor a 1 indica que la empresa tiene suficiente liquidez para cubrir sus deudas a corto plazo, lo cual es vital para la solvencia inmediata. Margen Neto Definición : Representa el porcentaje de ingresos que se convierten en beneficios netos después de deducir todos los costos y gastos. Importancia : Indica la eficiencia en la gestión de costos y la capacidad de la empresa para generar ganancias a partir de sus ingresos. Margen de EBITDA Definición : Mide la rentabilidad operativa de una empresa antes de intereses, impuestos, depreciación y amortización. Importancia : Proporciona una visión de la rentabilidad operativa sin los efectos de las decisiones financieras y contables, permitiendo comparaciones más justas entre empresas. Debt to Asset Ratio Definición : Indica qué proporción de los activos de una empresa está financiada con deuda. Importancia : Ayuda a evaluar el nivel de apalancamiento y el riesgo financiero de la empresa. Un ratio alto puede indicar una dependencia excesiva de la deuda para financiar activos. ‍ Consulta que es una persona moral acá . ‍ Extracción de Información Adicional ‍ Además de las métricas financieras, el OCR de Estados Financieros de Trébol puede extraer información crucial como: Tipo de Norma Contable : Identificación de si los estados financieros siguen NIIF, GAAP u otras normas locales, esencial para el análisis correcto y la comparabilidad internacional. Estados Financieros Auditados : Detección de si los estados han sido auditados y por qué firma, lo que aporta confianza y credibilidad a la información financiera presentada. ‍ Prevalidación de Documentos: Garantizando la Relevancia y Precisión ‍ Antes de procesar un documento, es esencial prevalidar que el PDF sea realmente un estado financiero. Esto asegura que: Relevancia de los Datos : Solo se procesan documentos pertinentes, evitando resultados erróneos o análisis inapropiados. Eficiencia Operativa : Se optimiza el uso de recursos al evitar el procesamiento de documentos irrelevantes. Calidad de la Información : Se garantiza que los datos extraídos sean precisos y aplicables al análisis financiero. La prevalidación utiliza algoritmos que analizan características específicas del documento, como encabezados, terminología financiera y estructuras típicas de estados financieros. ‍ APIs de Extracción de Datos de Estados Financieros ‍ Para maximizar la eficiencia y funcionalidad del OCR de Estados Financieros de Trébol, es crucial que pueda integrarse fácilmente con otros sistemas y plataformas a través de APIs (Interfaces de Programación de Aplicaciones). Esta conectividad permite: Automatización de Flujos de Trabajo : Los datos extraídos pueden ser enviados automáticamente a sistemas de gestión financiera, ERPs, CRMs y otras herramientas empresariales. Escalabilidad : Facilita el manejo de grandes volúmenes de datos al permitir que múltiples sistemas accedan y utilicen la información extraída simultáneamente. title: Five Key Findings From The Forrester Wave™: Workday Services, Q2 2026
summary: The Forrester Wave™: Workday Services, Q2 2026 reveals how AI, industry expertise, and continuous value realization are reshaping the Workday services market.
body_text: The Workday services market has entered a new phase. Buyers are no longer looking solely for implementation partners that can deliver projects on time and on budget. Increasingly, they want strategic partners that can help them drive continuous transformation, operationalize AI, and maximize platform value long after go-live. In The Forrester Wave™ Workday Services, Q2 2026 , we evaluated 14 of the most significant Workday services providers to help organizations identify the right partners for their needs. Here are five themes that stood out during our research: Workday services has become an AI-led transformation market The strongest providers are positioning Workday as a platform for enterprise transformation rather than simply an HR or finance system. Leaders increasingly differentiate themselves through AI-enabled consulting, proprietary accelerators, industry-specific AI solutions, agent-based automation, and innovation programs aligned to Workday’s product roadmap. Continuous value has replaced the traditional implementation mindset Workday customers are looking beyond deployment. Leading providers are expanding their focus to optimization, adoption, release management, managed services, and ongoing business transformation. Many firms now emphasize long-term value realization and continuous improvement as core elements of their strategy. Industry expertise is becoming a key differentiator As Workday expands deeper into finance, planning, payroll, workforce management, and industry-specific use cases, buyers increasingly value providers that bring deep industry knowledge. Healthcare, financial services, public sector, retail, and utilities customers often seek specialized operating models, regulatory expertise, and prebuilt industry solutions that accelerate time to value. Talent and delivery models matter more than ever The most successful providers have invested heavily in Workday-certified talent, global delivery capabilities, governance frameworks, and quality controls. In an increasingly competitive labor market, the ability to attract, develop, and retain Workday expertise remains one of the strongest predictors of execution success. Boutique firms continue to play an important role While global systems integrators dominate large-scale enterprise transformations, specialized boutique partners remain highly relevant, particularly for midmarket organizations and customers seeking deep functional expertise. Many boutiques compete effectively through governance, customer intimacy, innovation, and specialized Workday capabilities. This trend first emerged in our earlier evaluation and continues to shape the market today. What This Means For Buyers Selecting a Workday partner is no longer simply about implementation capacity. Organizations should evaluate providers based on their ability to support business transformation, leverage AI responsibly, deliver industry-specific expertise, and provide a roadmap for continuous value realization. The best partner for a global finance transformation may not be the same provider best suited for a midmarket human capital management deployment or a highly regulated industry environment. As Workday expands its footprint across HR, finance, planning, payroll, and AI-enabled workflows, the distinction between technology implementation and business transformation continues to blur. Buyers that align partner selection with their long-term transformation objectives will be best positioned to realize the full value of their Workday investment. title: SA-2026-087 - ExtremeXOS Debug-Mode Privilege Escalation via Weak PRNG (CVE-2026-8169)
summary: ExtremeXOS uses a challenge-response mechanism to authorize access to the privileged debug-mode function. The challenge value is generated using an insufficiently random source, which under certain conditions may allow an attacker to predict the expected response and activate debug-mode without authorization. Depending on device configuration and version, this may enable escalation to root-level access and persistent modification of the device software stack. Exploitation requires either a valid low-privilege account on the device (remote scenario) or physical serial console access (local scenario). Extreme would like to thank Hadrien Barral (Université Gustave Eiffel) and Georges-Axel Jaloyan (French Ministry of the Interior) for responsible disclosure of their findings. Products not listed in the Impact Details section have not been evaluated. Furthermore, products that have exceeded any software maintenance time periods are also not evaluated and will not be published. Please consult End of Sale and End of Service Life - Extreme Networks for the EOL notices related to the product under question.
